Article Title: Mamata Banerjee's Rejinagar pick withdraws from bypolls contest, then retracts
Article Text:
Mamata Banerjee faces setback in Rejinagar as her candidate withdraws.

Candidate changes his mind

Nandigram setback came first

TMC split complicates bypoll battle

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction's candidate for the Rejinagar Assembly bypoll, changed his decision to quit the contest on Saturday, saying he would remain in the race after Banerjee asked him to continue.Chowdhury, a former TMC MLA, had announced his withdrawal earlier in the day, citing difficulties in protecting party workers and introducing voters to the faction's newly allotted 'footballer' symbol.Hours later, he held another press conference and said he had reversed his decision after speaking to Banerjee and receiving assurances of security from the police.Chowdhury told news agency PTI at his home in Murshidabad earlier on Saturday, "It is becoming difficult for me to motivate grassroots workers who have been facing regular harassment. Also, it is an onerous task to familiarise the electorate with the new 'footballer' symbol in such a short time. In this given situation, last night I informed Mamata di about my decision (not to contest)... Let's see," he said.Later, he announced that he would contest the October 6 bypoll."I will be contesting the bypoll. I have been assured of security by the police after the supremo (Banerjee) intervened... I had a conversation with our party chief, who directed me not to quit the poll fray.I have met officers of the Beldanga police station and they have also assured me and my cadre of security during campaigning.""I am retracting from my earlier decision. I will see to it that none of our workers faces torture. Even if I have 10 activists, I will win," he added.The confusion in Rejinagar came a day after the Mamata faction suffered a setback in Nandigram, where its candidate Sanchita Pradhan Dey withdrew her nomination shortly before the deadline.Dey had met West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari at the state secretariat Nabanna along with her husband Satyajit before pulling out. She had lost her job in connection with a teacher recruitment scam. The reason for her withdrawal was not immediately clear.With no candidate left, Banerjee announced support for Congress nominee Milan Pradhan, calling the Congress a "sister party" and saying the move was aimed at strengthening the INDIA bloc ahead of the October 6 bypoll.Pradhan was later arrested in connection with criminal cases filed against him during the 2007 anti-land acquisition movement in Nandigram.The developments have unfolded amid a bitter dispute within the Trinamool Congress over its name and traditional 'flowers-and-grass' symbol.The Election Commission has allotted Banerjee's faction the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' and the 'footballer' symbol. The rival faction led by Arup Roy has been given the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and the 'envelope' symbol.Banerjee's camp accused the BJP government of "acting in an authoritarian manner to crush dissent and win the bypoll by a huge margin".BJP leader and Union minister Sukanta Majumdar rejected the charge, saying such allegations were expected from a "party centred on one person, whose activists had carried out attacks on the then opposition BJP after the 2021 assembly polls".With Chowdhury now back in the contest, the Mamata faction has retained its candidate in Rejinagar, while the Nandigram contest remains shaped by the withdrawal of its original nominee and its subsequent support for the Congress candidate.
Article Summary: Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction's candidate for the Rejinagar Assembly bypoll, changed his decision to quit the contest on Saturday. He had announced his withdrawal earlier in the day, citing difficulties in protecting party workers and introducing voters to the faction's newly allotted 'footballer' symbol. He later announced that he would contest the October 6 bypoll.

Article Title: Court questions transfer of cases against Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma
Article Text:
The court sought an action taken report from the SHO of Cyber police station

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has sought reports from Delhi Police on pleas filed by activist Harsh Mander seeking action against Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma and BJP MP Nishikant Dubey over alleged hate speech.The court sought an action taken report from the SHO of Cyber police station on a plea seeking registration of an FIR against Sarma. It also summoned the SHO of Malviya Nagar police station to explain the transfer of the complaint.In a separate matter concerning Dubey, it summoned the SHOs of Welcome and Bhajanpura police stations to appear on Oct 13 and explain the repeated transfer of a complaint seeking registration of an FIR against the BJP MP. Both matters have been listed for Oct 13.
Article Summary: A Delhi court has sought reports from Delhi Police on pleas filed by activist Harsh Mander. Mander sought action against Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma and BJP MP Nishikant Dubey over alleged hate speech. The court sought an action taken report from the SHO of Cyber police station.

Article Title: ‘BJP will seek equal seat-sharing in Punjab’: Hardeep Puri amid SAD alliance buzz
Article Text:
Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri (File photo)

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Union minister and BJP leader Hardeep Singh Puri said on Saturday the party would seek an equal seat-sharing agreement with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) if the two parties form an alliance for the upcoming Punjab assembly elections .“The earlier 22-seat formula will no longer work. The BJP will not play the role of a junior partner,” he told reporters in Amritsar, referring to the previous arrangement under which the BJP contested 22-23 of Punjab’s 117 assembly seats, while the SAD contested the remaining seats.A meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal in August had sparked speculation that the two former allies could renew their union. The SAD had ended its alliance with the BJP in 2020 in protest against the Centre’s contentious farm laws, which were subsequently repealed.Meanwhile, Puri also asserted that the BJP would leave “no stone unturned” to eradicate the drug menace in Punjab. He said the BJP-led government at the Centre was working on a “war footing” to create employment opportunities for unemployed youth in the state.Taking aim at the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Puri claimed that Punjab had reached a “bad situation” under chief minister Bhagwant Mann’s government, alleging “misrule” in the state.“People are feeling insecure. The police, whose job is to protect the public, are themselves feeling insecure,” the Union minister added.
Article Summary: BJP leader Hardeep Singh Puri says party will seek equal seat-sharing agreement with Shiromani Akali Dal. Meeting between PM Narendra Modi and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal in August had sparked speculation that the two former allies could renew their union.

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah suffered from food poisoning while on a visit to Karnataka on Saturday and skipped scheduled events in Hubballi and Belagavi, senior BJP leader and Union minister Pralhad Joshi said.Shah was scheduled to inaugurate the new academic building of KLE Jagadguru Gangadhar Mahaswamigalu Moorusavirmath Medical College and the 1,200-bed KLE Hospital and Medical Research Centre in Gabbur, Hubballi. "Naturally, due to vomiting from food poisoning, he had some weakness," he said.Shah's scheduled visit to Belagavi district was also cancelled. He was due to inaugurate the new headquarters building of Sri Beereshwara Cooperative Credit Society in Examba in Chikkodi taluk."Amit Shah should have come here. He suffered ill health due to food poisoning," Joshi told reporters at the event in Examba.Earlier, Joshi, Karnataka medical education minister Sharan Prakash Patil, former chief minister Basavaraj Bommai, Belagavi MP Jagadish Shettar and Sri Gurusiddha Rajayogindra Swami of Shri Jagadguru Moorusavirmath inaugurated the KLE campuses in Shah's absence.Shah had arrived in Hubballi late on Friday.

Article Title: System threatened by students as they ask questions: Rahul
Article Text:
The system wants ‘andh bhakts’, said Rahul

INDORE: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on Saturday said the "system" created by top BJP politicians and certain businessmen controlling every aspect of governance in the country is threatened by students.Addressing youth at a 'Chhatron ki Goonj' in Indore, he said, "The system is threatened by students as they ask questions. That is why the system does not want students. The system wants 'andh bhakts'." He described students as embodiments of curiosity, love, humility, courage, tolerance and honesty, while characterising blind followers as "delusional, hateful, arrogant, cowardly, patriarchal and dishonest".Rahul also targeted NSA Ajit Doval, accusing him of enabling "surveillance of citizens' communication data to help govt exert control over the population".
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi said the system is threatened by students as they ask questions. He described blind followers as "delusional, hateful, arrogant, cowardly, patriarchal and dishonest" He also targeted NSA Ajit Doval, accusing him of enabling surveillance of citizens' communication data.

Article Title: Mamata's 72-hour rollercoaster: Losing symbol, TMC name, candidate and then a breather on Day 3
Article Text:
Mamata's TMC rollercoaster: 3 days, 3 setbacks, then a breather

Day 1: EC freezes TMC name and symbol

Day 2: New name, new symbol, then Nandigram shock

Day 3: Rejinagar brings another scare, then a breather

NEW DELHI: Once the dominant political force in West Bengal, Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress is facing an unusual stretch of turbulence. Questions over the party's identity, leadership and organisational cohesion have all surfaced in the space of just 72 hours.For years, Mamata and the TMC have been almost synonymous in Bengal politics. But the past three days have brought one jolt after another, leaving the party dealing with a frozen identity, a new name and symbol, a candidate walking away in Nandigram and another nearly doing the same in Rejinagar.The first shock came when the Election Commission froze the TMC's familiar party name and its traditional 'flowers-and-grass' symbol amid the battle between Mamata Banerjee and the rival faction led by Arup Roy.The move was more than a technical setback for a party whose name and symbol have been central to its electoral identity for years.It also came after Mamata's stinging defeat at the hands of the BJP in the assembly polls, leaving the party vulnerable to rebellion and splits in both the state assembly and Parliament.The rebel faction had sought to stake its claim over the TMC's identity after 15 straight years of the party's rule in Bengal.The next day brought some clarity, but hardly any comfort for Didi.The Election Commission allotted the 'footballer' symbol to Mamata's faction and the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress'. The rival faction led by once-a-Didi-loyalist Arup Roy was given the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and the 'envelope' symbol.However, the drama for Didi went ahead to Nandigram seat.Sanchita Pradhan Dey, the TMC candidate in Nandigram, withdrew her nomination a day before the deadline after meeting Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, the BJP leader who had defeated Mamata in Nandigram.Dey, who had lost her job in connection with the teacher recruitment scam, met Adhikari along with her husband Satyajit before announcing her withdrawal. Her reasons were not immediately clear.The development left Mamata scrambling for a candidate in a constituency that is considered a Suvendu Adhikari bastion.Mamata then backed Congress candidate Milan Pradhan and described Congress as a "sister party", a move that also brought the INDIA bloc back into the picture ahead of the October 6 bypolls.But the reprieve was short-lived.Hours later, Milan Pradhan was arrested in connection with criminal cases linked to the 2007 anti-land acquisition movement in Nandigram, Purba Medinipur.The Mamata camp accused the BJP government of "acting in an authoritarian manner to crush dissent and win the bypoll by a huge margin".BJP leader and Union minister Sukanta Majumdar said such allegations were expected from a "party centred on one person, whose activists had carried out attacks on the then opposition BJP after the 2021 assembly polls".Just when the Nandigram episode seemed to have given Mamata enough to deal with, Rejinagar produced another surprise.Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the TMC candidate and former MLA, announced that he would withdraw from the bypoll, citing difficulties in motivating grassroots workers, police arrests and what he described as false cases against party workers. He also said familiarising voters with the new 'footballer' symbol in such a short time was proving difficult."It is becoming difficult for me to motivate grassroots workers who have been facing regular harassment. Police have arrested many of our workers, slapping false cases. Also, it is an onerous task to familiarise the electorate with the new 'footballer' symbol in such a short time. In this given situation, I informed Mamata di last evening about my decision (not to contest)... Let's see," he said.But within about 1.5 hours, the withdrawal itself was withdrawn."I will be contesting the bypoll. We are in Didi's party and we cannot do anything outside her wishes. So, following Didi's instructions, I am retaining my candidature," Chowdhury said.He said Mamata had directed him not to quit. He later visited Beldanga police station and said the police had assured him and his workers of security."I have been assured of security by the police after the supremo (Mamata) intervened. I have met officers of the Beldanga police station and they have also assured me and my cadre of security during campaigning," he said.Chowdhury also made it clear that he was ready to campaign with whoever remained with him."Even if only 10 workers stand by me, I will take them along and begin a door-to-door campaign," he said.For Mamata, it offered a small breather after two days of turbulence.The troubling sequence unfolded over 72 hours, turning into an unsettling rollercoaster for Didi.
Article Summary: Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress is facing an unusual stretch of turbulence. Questions over the party's identity, leadership and organisational cohesion have all surfaced. The past three days have brought one jolt after another, leaving the party dealing with a frozen identity, a new name and symbol.

Article Title: Rival TMC factions fight over control: Mamata submits three preferred names, symbols to EC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee registered her "strongest protest" after the Election Commission barred the rival factions from using party's name and reserved election symbol in the upcoming West Bengal Assembly bypolls, news agency PTI reported, citing sources."Mamata submitted response to EC's interim order seeking three preferred names, symbols "under strongest protest", at 11.36 pm on Thursday night," sources told PTI.This comes after the poll panel, in its interim order, ruled that neither faction can use AITC's name or "flowers and grass" symbol after acknowledging a split between factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Arup Roy.Both groups will have to contest the bypolls under different names and with election symbols allotted by the Commission. This arrangement will continue until the dispute is finally settled.EC said two rival groups each claimed to be the "real" party, requiring substantive determination under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. It said the interim measure, based on precedents, would place them on an "even keel".The poll panel has been hearing competing claims from the two factions over control of the party, its name and election symbol.Both sides have submitted documents and appeared before the Commission during the proceedings.The dispute reached the Election Commission in July after the rival factions staked competing claims to control of the TMC. The panel subsequently sought responses on issues including organisational control, authorised signatories, party assets, name and election symbol.
Article Summary: Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee registered her "strongest protest" after the Election Commission barred the rival factions from using party's name and reserved election symbol. This comes after the poll panel ruled that neither faction can use AITC's name or "flowers and grass" symbol.

Article Title: 'BJP and EC join forces to split party': Rahul Gandhi slams EC over TMC name, symbol freeze

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Friday slammed the Election Commission for barring TMC from using party name and symbol in the upcoming assembly bypolls in West Bengal, accusing the poll panel and Bharatiya Janata Party of joining forces to split a party.In a social media post on X, Rahul pointed towards the past examples of split in shiv Sena and NCP."First Shiv Sena, then NCP, and now Trinamool Congress . Every time, the same pattern—BJP and the Election Commission join forces to split a party. Then its election symbol is snatched away," the Congress leader said."When an entire party can be stolen, it's hardly surprising that the votes of millions of Indians can be stolen too," he added.Rahul also said that "vote chori, sarkaar chori and now party chori have become the symbols of democratic decline" in the country."Vote theft. Government theft. Now party theft—these have become symbols of our democratic decline. The ECI's constitutional responsibility is to protect the mandate—but instead, it's aiding those very forces that overturn the people's verdict," the Congress leader said."This fight isn't just Mamata Banerjee's. It's the fight of every political party, every voter who wants free and fair elections," he added.Rahul's remarks came after the poll panel, in its interim order, ruled that neither faction of TMC can use its name or "flowers and grass" symbol after acknowledging a split between factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Arup Roy.Both groups will have to contest the bypolls under different names and with election symbols allotted by the Commission. This arrangement will continue until the dispute is finally settled.EC said two rival groups each claimed to be the "real" party, requiring substantive determination under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. It said the interim measure, based on precedents, would place them on an "even keel".Meanwhile, West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh claimed that TMC is crumbling under the weight of severe internal strife following the Election Commission's interim order."The Trinamool Congress (TMC) is disintegrating due to internal infighting. The public has rejected them. Their MPs are in other parties, and Mamata Banerjee stands alone. They hold no documents regarding this; the Election Commission will make the decision," he said.The poll panel has been hearing competing claims from the two factions over control of the party, its name and election symbol. Both sides have submitted documents and appeared before the Commission during the proceedings.The dispute reached the Election Commission in July after the rival factions staked competing claims to control of the TMC. The panel subsequently sought responses on issues including organisational control, authorised signatories, party assets, name and election symbol.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi slams Election Commission for barring TMC from using party name and symbol. Accuses poll panel and Bharatiya Janata Party of joining forces to split a party. West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh claims that TMC is crumbling under the weight of severe internal strife.

Article Title: How dating app turned into an extortion trap
Article Text:
(AI image used) After meeting a woman via a dating app, a man became a victim of an alleged extortion plot





NEW DELHI: A conversation on a dating app led a 44-year-old man to Dhansa metro station, but what began as a routine meeting soon turned into an alleged extortion trap. Delhi Police said the man was allegedly threatened and forced to part with Rs 2.15 lakh.The alleged trap was set through an app. According to police, the woman who contacted the complainant called him to Dhansa metro station and took him to premises in Najafgarh. Once inside, he was allegedly threatened, while one of the accused allegedly posed as a police officer to intimidate him.The complainant approached Chhawla police station on Sept 14, following which an FIR was registered.Police said the alleged extortion involved Rs 1.93 lakh transferred through bank-to-bank and UPI transactions and another Rs 22,000 paid in cash. Investigators traced the digital trail and identified the bank accounts through which the money had moved.DCP (Dwarka) Kushal Pal Singh said four people, Mandeep (38), Preeti (32), Kamlesh (42) and Ritu (40), have been arrested; cops said around Rs 70,500 has been recovered, while the remaining amount traced to the concerned bank accounts has been frozen.Among those arrested, Mandeep allegedly has previous cases registered against him in Sonipat and Delhi, including cases under provisions relating to extortion and criminal intimidation. Police said Kamlesh was also previously involved in a case registered at Dwarka North police station.
Article Summary: The alleged trap was set through an app. The woman who contacted the complainant called him to Dhansa metro station and took him to premises in Najafgarh. Once inside, he was allegedly threatened, while one of the accused allegedly posed as a police officer to intimidate him. Police said the alleged extortion involved Rs 1.93 lakh transferred through bank-to-bank and UPI transactions.

Article Title: EC freezes TMC name and symbol, asks rival camps for options
Article Text:
In Photo: Former CM Mamata Banerjee; Ritabrata Banerjee

Other knots





KOLKATA: Election Commission on Thursday issued an interim order freezing the name ‘ All India Trinamool Congress ’ and the party’s ‘flowers and grass’ symbol.The full bench of the poll panel, chaired by chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, directed the rival camps in the party — one headed by former CM Mamata Banerjee and the other by the leader of opposition in the assembly, Ritabrata Banerjee — to submit three choices for a party name and as many for an election symbol by 11am on Friday for the Oct 6 bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar. The EC will allot a name and a symbol from the lists to each camp.The order signals a major shift in Bengal politics after 28 years. For the first time since Jan 1998, when Mamata broke away from Congress to form her own party, neither the name ‘All India Trinamool Congress’ nor its flowers-and-grass symbol will feature on EVMs in Bengal. The party, which governed the state for a decade and a half, was trounced by BJP in this year’s assembly polls, leading to a split in the once formidable organisation.EC’s 14-page order reasoned that an interim order was necessary because “the time available is not adequate to complete the proceedings under Para 15 of the Symbols Order”, given that the bypolls are less than three weeks away. Stating that the claims by the rival blocs required a “substantive determination”, the EC order said the interim decision would “cover the purpose of the current bye-elections and continue till the final determination of the dispute”.The ruling specified: “Neither of the two groups led by Shri Arup Roy (Petitioner) and other led by Ms. Mamata Banerjee (Respondent) shall be permitted to use the name of the party ‘All India Trinamool Congress’ simplicitor, nor use the symbol ‘Flowers & Grass’.” It added: “Both the groups shall be known by such names as they may choose for their respective groups, including, if they so desire, linkage with their parent party ‘All India Trinamool Congress’. ”The factions, EC said, “were asked to submit three options, in order of preference, for both their group names and free symbols”.Trinamool MP Kalyan Banerjee, who represented Mamata at Thursday’s hearings, called the order “unacceptable”. Asked about the camp’s next move, he said, “We have a long time, till 11 am on Friday, to decide.”Ritabrata said, “Trinamool is not anyone’s fief. We will decide our course of action tomorrow.”EC’s decision aligns with precedents. Ahead of the Oct 2022 Andheri East assembly bypoll, EC froze the ‘Shiv Sena’ name and its ‘Bow and Arrow’ symbol for both factions — headed by Udhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde. In Oct 2021, following the death of Ram Vilas Paswan, EC froze his party’s name — ‘Lok Janshakti Party’ — and its reserved ‘Bungalow’ symbol.Earlier on Thursday, the returning officers (ROs) in Nandigram and Rejinagar adjourned the scrutiny of nominations filed by candidates fielded by the rival Trinamool camps to Friday. The move followed a submission by Congress that the nominations should be rejected because each had only one proposer.“After informing EC of the matter, the ROs adjourned the scrutiny until Friday under Section 36 of Representation of the People Act. The ROs will resume the process at 11 am,” an EC official said.Before the order was released, a five-member delegation from the Mamata camp met with the poll panel. After the meeting, Mamata loyalist Kalyan said, “We presented our arguments. The claim that Trinamool working committee ceased to exist in 2025 is false.”He was responding to arguments from the Ritabrata faction that Trinamool’s national working committee, which was formed in February 2022 and had a tenure of three years, had expired in February 2025. The faction also cited a July 2026 ex-parte interim injunction from an Alipore court regarding the control of TMC offices, bank accounts and other assets.Ritabrata, who also led a five-member delegation to EC, said after the meeting: “We have presented our case and answered all queries. We have left the decision regarding the party symbol to EC and are 100% confident the verdict will be in our favour.”
Article Summary: The order signals a major shift in Bengal politics after 28 years. Neither the name ‘All India Trinamool Congress’ nor its flowers-and-grass symbol will feature on EVMs in Bengal. The party, which governed the state for a decade and a half, was trounced by BJP.

Article Title: Delhi Rk Puram Accident: Watch: Car hits bike, drags it for 100 metres on Delhi road; driver held
Article Text:
In video, a parked motorcycle was hit by a car, which then pulled the bike along for 100 meters





NEW DELHI: A car dragged a parked motorcycle for about 100 metres after hitting it on Africa Avenue Road near R K Puram Metro Station on Wednesday night, police said.The motorcyclist, identified as 21-year-old Tanish Tokas, fell from the bike but escaped serious injury, while the driver, identified as 73-year-old Venu Gopal, was arrested.The incident took place around 10pm on September 17 when Tokas, a resident of Munirka Village, was sitting on his parked black motorcycle on the roadside. Gopal, a resident of Vasant Kunj, was travelling from Bhikaji Cama Place towards R K Puram Metro Station in a blue Honda Amaze when the car hit the motorcycle.Tokas fell from the motorcycle after the impact, while the bike was dragged for about 100 metres. Tokas himself was not dragged by the car, police said.Police received information about the accident at around 10.22pm and reached the spot. The Honda Amaze was seized and Gopal was apprehended during the investigation.A case under sections 281 and 125(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita has been registered at R K Puram police station. Gopal was medically examined and no alcohol was detected, police said.
Article Summary: A car dragged a parked motorcycle for about 100 metres after hitting it on Africa Avenue Road near R K Puram Metro Station. The motorcyclist, 21-year-old Tanish Tokas, fell from the bike but escaped serious injury. Driver Venu Gopal, 73, was arrested.

Article Title: Man held for killing co-worker after drunken brawl
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:

Three held in separate narcotics cases

Kolhapur:





A 40-year-old man was allegedly murdered by his co-worker at a scrap godown in Sangavdewadi near Gokul Shirgaon on Wednesday night following a drunken altercation.The deceased, Utkarsh Hanmantrao Bhosle (40) of Belagavi (Karnataka) and the accused, Suhas Dilip Dudhade of Kalgav in Satara’s Karad taluka, worked together at the godown.Police said the two had consumed alcohol when an argument broke out after Bhosle allegedly refused to share a cellphone number for making a call. The dispute escalated into a scuffle, during which Dudhade allegedly picked up an iron bar lying on the premises and struck Bhosle on the head. Bhosle suffered severe injuries and died before he could receive medical treatment.Gokul Shirgaon police arrested Dudhade at the scene. He was later produced before a court, which remanded him to five days of police custody, said sub-inspector M Rajput.Local crime branch has arrested Sangram Bhagiratram Dara (30) Jodhpur (Rajasthan) from Kaneriwadi and seized 7kg of opium powder worth Rs 1 lakh.Dara, who works with a transport firm, was arrested following a tip-off. A case has been registered at Gokul Shirgaon police station.In another case, police seized 28g of mephedrone worth Rs 5.04 lakh and arrested Pintu alias Dhanaji Pandurang Jadhav (34) of Shahapur, Ichalkaranji, and Siddharth Bade of Ichalkaranji, allegedly the supplier. The case has been registered at Shahapur police station under sections 8(c), 22(b) and 29 of the NDPS Act, said assistant sub-inspector Avinash Mungase.
Article Summary: A 40-year-old man was allegedly murdered by his co-worker at a scrap godown in Sangavdewadi near Gokul Shirgaon on Wednesday night. The deceased, Utkarsh Hanmantrao Bhosle (40) of Belagavi (Karnataka) and the accused, Suhas Dilip Dudhade of Kalgav in Satara’s Karad taluka, worked together.

Article Title: Speeding SUV hits bike in Vashi, 3 youths injured; driver traced
Article Text:
Accused driver of SUV Mahindra Thar escaping after accident





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday.The incident took place around 1am. The injured youths were initially taken to NMMC Hospital in Vashi and were later referred to Sion Hospital for further treatment.Following the incident, a biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police then traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number.During the investigation, it was learnt that the owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride. Police subsequently traced his mobile tower location to an area near the creek in Sector 12, Vashi, where he was allegedly hiding.He was detained and served a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following which he was released.
Article Summary: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday. A biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number. The owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride.

Article Title: Quack doctor detained in Maharashtra for practising medicine without registration
Article Text:
A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel police after an inspection (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel taluka police after a complaint was lodged by the medical officer of the Primary Health Centre at Ajivali village in Panvel taluka, following an inspection by health department officials at his illegal clinic in Kasalkhand village on Monday afternoon.The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal and resides in an MHADA building in India Bulls Township, Kon village, Panvel.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of Panvel taluka police, informed that the complaint was lodged by medical officer Dr Sayali Mankar, 33, who inspected Haq's clinic in Kasalkhand village and found that he was an unqualified and unregistered medical practitioner allegedly practising modern medicine by posing as a doctor.He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.Inspector Ghadge said, "We have invoked relevant sections of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, 1961, against the accused, which prohibit any person from practising medicine in the state unless their name is registered under the relevant statutory provisions and prescribe criminal penalties and fines for those who illegally practise medicine without valid registration. Under the law, the accused was served a notice under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directing him to appear for inquiry when summoned and during the court proceedings. "
Article Summary: The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal. He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: Cong neta seeks protection for 'gangrape' survivor, her kin
Article Text:
(Representative image)





THANE: A day after Padgha police registered an FIR against former Kalyan West MLA Narendra Pawar and dismissed policeman Shailesh Patil for allegedly gangraping a 22-year-old married woman at a farmhouse in Bapgaon, Congress group leader in KDMC Kanchan Kulkarni on Friday sought police protection for the survivor and her family.Kulkarni, who accompanied the woman to the police station, claimed the survivor's life was in danger because of the accused's influence. She urged CM Eknath Shinde to intervene and ensure security for her.Meanwhile, Padgha police conducted a spot panchnama at the farmhouse in Bapgaon to collect forensic evidence. Seperate police teams have also been formed to trace Pawar and Patil, who remain absconding. Pawar has denied the charge, calling them false. He has also resigned from all his BJP organisational posts. - Pradeep Gupta
Article Summary: Congress group leader in KDMC Kanchan Kulkarni sought police protection for the survivor and her family. She urged CM Eknath Shinde to intervene and ensure security for her. Padgha police conducted a spot panchnama at the farmhouse in Bapgaon to collect forensic evidence.

Article Title: Cops slap MCOCA on 5-member Butibori gang for armed robbery
Article Text: Nagpur: The Nagpur Rural Police have invoked Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against a five-member gang accused of armed robbery and spreading terror in the Butibori area.Acting on the directions of Senior Superintendent of Police Harrsh A Poddar and Additional SP Anil Mhaske, Butibori police charged gang leader Dikshant Patil (26) of Video Chowk and members Amit alias Nana Bhoyar (26), Devsingh Bhatti (23), Ashish alias Muchyu Karale (26) and Kunal Purke (28).The case was registered at Bori police station after complainant Om Raju Basne alleged that on Aug 26, the accused intercepted him on Satgaon Road near Ai Lawn, threatened him with a knife, tied his hands with rope, abused him and robbed him of Rs4,500 in cash, an iPhone, Rs2,000 transferred online and his motorcycle.Police seized the knife, iron rod, rope and mobiles. Four accused have been arrested. Investigators found that the group had a record of robbery, assault and intimidation.
Article Summary: Nagpur Rural Police have invoked Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against a five-member gang accused of armed robbery and spreading terror. The case was registered at Bori police station after complainant Om Raju Basne alleged that on Aug 26, the accused intercepted him on Satgaon Road near Ai Lawn.

Article Title: Phone link goof-up costs woman Ladki Bahin monthly dole
Article Text:
Amravati:





A 41-year-old woman from Nandgaon Khandeshwar in Amravati district was allegedly deprived of benefits under the state govt’s ‘Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana’ after her mobile number was found linked to the Registration Certificate (RC) of her neighbour’s four-wheeler.The error came to light after the beneficiary noticed that the monthly financial assistance under the scheme had abruptly stopped. Upon inquiry, she found that govt verification records showed a four-wheeler registered in her name, making her ineligible as per the scheme’s norms that exclude families owning a four-wheeler.On further verification, it was revealed that the vehicle, purchased in 2018, belongs to a 70-year-old woman living next to the complainant’s house. However, the complainant’s mobile number was linked to the car’s RC.The woman has alleged that her mobile number was used and linked to the vehicle records without her knowledge or consent, due to which she was disqualified from the scheme despite not owning any vehicle.Following her complaint, Nandgaon Khandeshwar police registered a case on Wednesday and started an investigation.Confirming the development, the police station officer Anand Pidurkar said, “We have registered a case based on the woman’s complaint. Her mobile number is mentioned in the RC records of her neighbour’s four-wheeler. We are investigating who provided the number, why it was entered, and what the motive was behind it.”Police said they are examining the RTO records and the role of the persons involved in the registration process.
Article Summary: A 41-year-old woman from Nandgaon Khandeshwar in Amravati district was allegedly deprived of benefits under the state govt’s ‘Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana’ Her mobile number was found linked to the Registration Certificate (RC) of her neighbour's four-wheeler.

Article Title: Govt psychiatrist arrested in wife’s suicide case
Article Text:
Bombay HC rejected psychiatrist’s anticipatory bail plea on Sept 11

Nashik

:





Police on Friday arrested govt psychiatrist Dr Nilesh Jejurkar in connection with the death of his wife and ayurveda practitioner, Manisha (40), who was found hanging at the couple’s residence in the Gangapur Road area on March 6.According to police, Jejurkar has been booked for abetment of suicide under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). On March 8, Manisha’s sister had lodged a complaint alleging that Jejurkar was responsible for her death.Following the registration of the case, Jejurkar sought anticipatory bail before a Nashik sessions court, which rejected his plea. He subsequently moved Bombay high court and continued working at Nashik Civil Hospital while his application was pending.On Sept 11, Bombay HC rejected his anticipatory bail plea, observing that a prima facie case indicating mens rea and harassment had been made out against the applicant. The court also noted that certain circumstances raised questions that could potentially point to murder rather than suicide.Complainant’s counsel, advocate Abhaysinh Bhosale, said Jejurkar then challenged the HC order before Supreme Court through a special leave petition (SLP). A bench of justices Satish Chandra Sharma and Nongmeikapam Kotiswar Singh, however, declined to interfere with the HC order and dismissed the petition.
Article Summary: Police on Friday arrested govt psychiatrist Dr Nilesh Jejurkar in connection with the death of his wife and ayurveda practitioner, Manisha (40), who was found hanging at the couple’s residence in the Gangapur Road area on March 6. On Sept 11, Bombay HC rejected his anticipatory bail plea, observing that a prima facie case indicating mens rea had been made out against the applicant.

Article Title: Dharapuram bypoll: Nine AIADMK functionaries booked for attack on TVK candidate’s car
Article Text: TIRUPUR: Police have registered a case against AIADMK candidate K Bhanumathi and eight party functionaries following a complaint alleging that the car of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) candidate P Sathyabama was intercepted and damaged after she filed her nomination papers for the Oct 6 Dharapuram byelection.Besides Bhanumathi, Dharapuram police booked former ministers Pollachi V Jayaraman and Dindigul C Sreenivasan, and party functionaries Senthilkumar, Rajendran, Deepa, Gomathi, Rani and Muthumani. Police have invoked 10 sections, including provisions relating to insulting a woman, damaging private property and acts allegedly intended to provoke violence or rioting.The complaint was lodged by Gayathri, treasurer of the TVK’s 18th ward in Dharapuram, on Thursday. She alleged that AIADMK functionaries, who had come to file nominations, stopped Sathyabama’s car while she was returning from the nomination centre.According to the complaint, the AIADMK functionaries damaged the vehicle and used abusive and derogatory language against the TVK candidate. It alleged that their actions were aimed at provoking clashes between AIADMK and TVK supporters.
Article Summary: Police have registered a case against AIADMK candidate K Bhanumathi and eight party functionaries. A complaint alleges that the car of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) candidate P Sathyabama was intercepted and damaged after she filed her nomination papers for the Oct 6 Dharapuram byelection.

Article Title: Auto driver arrested for threatening, assaulting cops in Yercaud
Article Text:
Representative image





SALEM: The Yercaud police have arrested an autorickshaw driver on charges of assaulting a special sub-inspector (SSI) and threatening to kill the SSI and a woman police constable.The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. Yuvraj, who was drunk, obstructed vehicles near a Vinayagar statue on Monday. Head constable D Thavamani, who was regulating traffic, intervened. Yuvraj abused her verbally.SSI Aaron Athirubaraj attempted to defuse the situation. “But Yuvraj tore my shirt, struck me on the chest and threatened to kill me and Thavamani,” the SSI said.Police registered a case against Yuvraj under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. He was remanded in judicial custody. Police registered a case against him under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation.

Article Title: Arrest of Congress candidate in Bengal one of democracy’s darkest chapters: K C Venugopal
Article Text:
AICC general secretary K C Venugopal

Kottayam:





AICC general secretary K C Venugopal has described the police action against Congress candidate Milan Pradhan in Nandigram, West Bengal, as one of the ‘darkest chapters’ in Indian democracy, saying it amounts to a direct challenge to a candidate’s right to contest elections freely.Speaking to reporters in Alappuzha on Saturday, Venugopal said it was Congress, not CPM, that was taking on BJP in the country, alleging that basic democratic freedoms no longer existed and that dissenting voices were being entangled in fabricated cases. He claimed the country was being turned into a ‘banana republic’ and predicted BJP would be voted out in 2029.Venugopal said that the police took Pradhan into custody citing a case linked to the 2007 Nandigram agitation, within an hour of the Trinamool Congress candidate’s withdrawal and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee ’s announcement of support for the Congress nominee. He said election commission ’s silence over opposition candidates being unable to file nominations or campaign independently was a matter of serious concern.Venugopal alleged that West Bengal Police pressured Pradhan to withdraw his candidature in exchange for relief in existing cases and other benefits, but that the candidate had refused, saying he would not withdraw “even at the cost of his life”. He said the party was proud of Pradhan’s courage and democratic conviction.He added that the Pradesh Congress Committee president, senior AICC functionaries and he himself had remained in touch with Pradhan and his family through the night, and that the party would extend full support to them.Venugopal said Congress, under Rahul Gandhi, was waging an uncompromising fight against what it called BJP’s anti-democratic conduct, both inside and outside Parliament, and that the Nandigram episode would be escalated into a nationwide protest. He said the party would review its electoral performance and organisational matters but would not compromise on its fight for democratic rights and justice.
Article Summary: AICC general secretary K C Venugopal has described the police action against Congress candidate Milan Pradhan in Nandigram, West Bengal, as one of the ‘darkest chapters’ in Indian democracy. He said it amounts to a direct challenge to a candidate’s right to contest elections freely.
